summary: This page presents the main portfolio overview for AA REIT, featuring a table detailing the asset split by region (Australia and Singapore) with property counts and portfolio value percentages. The content describes the nature of assets across five categories—Logistics, Warehouse, Business Parks, Industrial, and Hi-Tech—and notes that the total portfolio is valued at S$2.13 billion as of 31 March 2025.

This page presents the FY2025 key financial and operational highlights for AA REIT, featuring a "Resilient Financial Performance" table reporting gross revenue of S$186.6 million and distributions to unitholders of S$78.2 million in SGD'000s. Additional sections detail asset management metrics including 93.6% portfolio occupancy, strong balance sheet data showing 28.9% gearing, and sustainability initiatives such as rooftop solar panel installation across 3 properties.

This page presents the Financial Highlights for SGX REIT, displaying tables and charts for Gross Revenue, Net Property Income, Distributions to Unitholders, Distribution per Unit, Total Assets, and Net Asset Value per Unit in S$'million (except NAV per unit in S$). All metrics are reported for the financial years ending 31 March from 2021 through 2025.

This page presents the DPU and financial highlights for SGX REIT, displaying Gross Revenue, Net Property Income, and Distribution per Unit (DPU) in S$ million across fiscal years 2021–2025 alongside a Balance Sheet showing Total Assets, Liabilities, and Unitholders' Funds. Key financial ratios including Net Asset Value per Unit, Aggregate Leverage Ratio, Interest Coverage Ratios, and Weighted Average All-in Cost of Debt are also provided with explanatory footnotes on their calculations and specific exclusions.

This page presents a flowchart illustrating the Trust Structure of AIMS APAC REIT, detailing the relationships between Unitholders, the Trust (AIMS AA REIT), The Manager (AIMS APAC REIT Management Limited*), The Trustee (HSBC Institutional Trust Services (Singapore) Limited), and various property and investment managers. The diagram explicitly maps the flows of Distributions, Holding of Units, Net Property Income, Ownership of Assets, and management fees across these entities without providing audited financial statements or specific monetary values.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Total Return for SGX REIT, reporting FY2025 and FY2024 financial highlights in SGD'000 including gross revenue, net property income, distributions to unitholders (S$78,154), and distribution per unit (DPU) at 9.600 Singapore cents. The accompanying text details that gross revenue increased by S$9.3 million primarily due to higher rental income from AA REIT's logistics properties, partially offset by losses from divestments and foreign exchange fluctuations.

This page details the financial components of the Profit or Loss, specifically highlighting Net Property Income of S$133.7 million for FY2025 and Borrowing Costs of S$37.5 million, alongside Manager's Management Fees, Performance Fees, Other Trust Expenses, and the Share of Joint Venture losses. It further reports on Fair Value changes in Investment Properties and Derivative Financial Instruments, a Gain on Divestment of Yishun Industrial Park A, and distribution terms for three tranches of Perpetual Securities issued by the Trust.

This page presents the DISTRIBUTIONS TO UNITHOLDERS, TOTAL ASSETS AND NET ASSET VALUE ("NAV") PER UNIT, and CASH FLOWS for AA REIT as of 31 March 2025, with financial figures reported in S$'000. The main artifact is the Consolidated statement of financial position table showing total assets at S\$2,290,620, net assets attributable to Unitholders at S\$1,005,891, and a NAV per Unit of S\$1.23.

This page presents the Capital Management section featuring two tables: a Key Financial Metrics table reporting Gross borrowings, Total Assets, Aggregate Leverage ratio, and Weighted Average All-in Cost of Debt as at 31 March 2025 (S$'million) alongside a Financial Flexibility & Liquidity table detailing Cash and bank balance and Undrawn committed facilities for the same period. The text details capital milestones including the issuance of SLLs and subordinated perpetual securities, notes that total gross borrowings decreased to S$582.4 million due to interim repayments and currency fluctuations, and outlines the full deployment of approximately S$100.0 million from the Equity Fund Raising launched in May 2023.

This page presents the **Aggregate Leverage Ratio** table for AA REIT covering FY 2021 to 2025, reporting Total Assets and Total Borrowings in **SGD'000**, alongside textual disclosures on capital management, perpetual securities, debt headroom, and financial flexibility as of 31 March 2025.

The page presents a **Debt Maturity Profile** table (S$ million) detailing AA REIT's debt expiring from FY 2026 to 2030, alongside a sensitivity analysis table showing interest coverage ratio ("ICR") impacts under EBITDA and interest rate variations as at 31 March 2025. No audited Portfolio Statement, Statement of Total Return, revenue/expense notes, tenant mix, DPU highlights, or manager/trustee/sponsor information are present; the reporting unit is explicitly stated as S$ million.

This page presents the "Top 10 Tenants by GRI" table detailing AA REIT's leading customers, their respective trade sectors, and weighted average lease expiry (WALE) years. It also includes a FY2025 Gross Rental Income (GRI) breakdown by asset class showing Logistics and Warehouse as the largest segment at 47.2% of GRI, alongside text describing active Asset Enhancement Initiative projects and tenant diversification across 13 industries.

This page presents the AA REIT Portfolio Review, featuring a **Tenant Trade by FY2025 GRI** table that details industry percentages (Logistics 28.5%, Food & Consumer Staples 18.4%) and highlights that 83.0% of Gross Rental Income comes from defensive and essential industries. It further includes occupancy metrics reporting a total portfolio rate of 93.6% as of 31 March 2025, with quarterly comparisons against the JTC Industrial Average and a breakdown by Singapore and Australia sub-portfolio.

This page details the Manager's lease activity and rental performance for FY2025, featuring a table titled "Rental Reversion for Singapore Assets (%)" that breaks down quarterly and annual reversion rates by property segment (Logistics & Warehouse, Industrial, Business Park) and portfolio average. The reporting unit is not explicitly stated in the text, so 'no schema-relevant data' applies to specific financial figures like revenue or expenses; however, key operational metrics include 75 new leases signed at 159,827 sqm with a weighted average term of 4.6 years and a portfolio-wide rental reversion of 20.0%.

This page presents the **audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations)** via a table detailing FY2026 to FY2030 lease expiry percentages by segment, reporting units in percentage of GRI. It also includes a donut chart and summary notes on the **trade/tenant mix** (41.9% single-tenant vs 58.1% multi-tenanted) and **DPU / distribution / financial highlights** regarding weighted average lease expiry of 4.4 years.

This page presents the Audited Portfolio Statement as of 31 March 2025, detailing a total property valuation of S$2,126.4 million (S$'000) comprising S$1,508.0 million in Singapore and S$618.4 million in Australia across 28 properties, alongside a table breaking down valuations by portfolio segment, location, and property type with comparative figures from March 2024. The content also includes a Land Lease Expiry artifact displaying weighted average lease durations and a stacked bar chart illustrating the distribution of portfolio value by years remaining on land leases across Logistics & Warehouse, Industrial, Business Park, and Hi-Tech categories.

This page presents the **Unit Price Performance** and **Monthly Trading Performance** of AA REIT for FY2025, featuring a table detailing monthly unit price changes against the FSTREI Index and Straits Times Index, alongside a table tracking total trading volume (in million units) and closing prices in S$. The reporting unit is explicitly stated as **S$** for currency and **million units** for trading volume.

This page presents the AA REIT Unit Price Performance and Total Unitholder Return tables, reporting unit price metrics (opening, closing, high, low, volume) and market capitalisation in S$' million for fiscal years 2021 through 2025. It also details comparative yield returns against indices and benchmarks as of 31 March 2025, including a specific note on the Distribution Per Unit (DPU) of 9.600 Singapore cents used to calculate the total unitholder return.

This page of the AA REIT annual report details the company's Investor Relations activities, including its policy, disclosure practices, engagement strategies, and recent Annual General Meeting proceedings. It presents Unitholders' Profile and Institutional Holders by Geography as at 31 March 2025 using pie charts and tables showing distribution percentages across categories and regions, with no audited Portfolio Statement, financial statements, or specific unit currency schema present.

This page displays the **Singapore Property Portfolio** map and list of 25 quality properties as at 31 March 2025, categorized by sector (Logistics & Warehouse, Industrial, Business Park, Hi-Tech) with specific addresses. No audited financial statements, tenant tables, or DPU data are present on this page.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) for Singapore properties as of 31 March 2025, listing 11 assets with details on lease terms, purchase and fair-value valuations in S$ million, NLA, gross rental income, and occupancy rates. It also includes summary metrics showing total portfolio valuation at S$945.1 million, gross rental income for FY2025 at S$85.9 million, and an overall occupancy rate of 92.4%.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement detailing 10 Singapore and 1 Australian properties with acquisition dates, land lease expiries, purchase prices, valuations as at 31 March 2025 (SGD'000), NLA, gross rental income for FY2025 (S$ million), and occupancy rates. The reporting unit is explicitly SGD'000 for the table data and S$ million for the summary highlights, which report a total Gross Rental Income of S$37.4 million and a total valuation of S$385.3 million against a portfolio NLA of 163,320 sqm.

This page presents the Audited Portfolio Statement for the SGX REIT's Business Park segment, detailing property valuations and financial metrics as of 31 March 2025 in SGD'000. The main artifact is a table listing two properties in Singapore and Australia with columns for lease type, acquisition date, land lease expiry, remaining term, purchase price, valuation, NLA, gross rental income, and occupancy rate, alongside summary icons showing total occupancy (93.9%), total NLA (102,384 sqm), gross rental income ($S$46.1 million), portfolio valuation ($S$647.6 million), and the percentage of portfolio by valuation (30.5%).

This page presents a single-property Statement of Portfolio for the Northtech building in Singapore, detailing its acquisition details, valuation of S$148.5 million (7.0% of portfolio), gross rental income of S$13.1 million for FY2025, and 99.8% occupancy as at 31 March 2025. The reporting unit is consistently expressed in S$ million.

This page presents Singapore's industrial production data through a table and chart titled "Singapore Index of Industrial Production, 4Q 2014 to 1Q 2025" showing year-on-year changes, alongside a table and chart for "Total FAI, 2014 to 2024" detailing Fixed Asset Investment by sector. The accompanying text provides narrative details on sector-specific growth and investment figures reported in S$ million (e.g., S\$13.5 billion total FAI in 2024) but does not contain audited financial statements, tenant tables, or DPU highlights.

This page presents sector analysis and outlooks for Singapore's logistics industry, featuring a table of total container volumes from 2014 to 2024 (in Tonnes '000) and a table of air cargo handled including imports, exports, and totals from 2014 to 2024 (in Tonnes '000), alongside text detailing future infrastructure plans and economic forecasts.

This page presents an overview of the Singapore industrial property market featuring a table detailing total industrial stock by type as at 1Q 2025 and narrative descriptions of major investment sale transactions totaling S$6.0 billion for the year, including specific deal values such as the S$1.4 billion divestment of KDC data centres and the S$1.6 billion acquisition by Lendlease and Warburg Pincus.

This page presents a table detailing private investment sales of Keppel Data Centres REIT's portfolio, listing building names such as Keppel Data Centres (KDC SGP 7 and KDC SGP 8) with transacted prices in SGD million, land areas, tenures, transaction periods, buyers, and sellers for Q1–Q4 2024. The data is sourced from the URA and Knight Frank Singapore, with a note defining private investment sales as transactions involving an entire building or bulk sales worth S$10 million or more.

This page presents market research on Singapore's private single-user factory segment, led by **Exhibit 5-1: Net new and potential supply of private single-user factory space, 2014 to 2028F**, which details annual supply figures in '000 sq ft. Additionally, **Exhibit 5-2: Notable upcoming completions of single-user factory space, 2025 to 2027** lists specific projects with their locations, developers, uncompleted gross floor area (GFA), and expected completion years.

This page features three key market data artifacts for JTC multiple-user factory space: Exhibit 5-8 detailing Net Demand and Occupancy (2014–1Q 2025) in '000 sq ft, Exhibit 5-9 presenting the Rental Index (base 4Q 2012=100), and Exhibit 5-10 showing the Price Index (base 4Q 2012=100). All tables report figures as indexed values or square footage units without specific financial currency reporting units such as SGD'000 or S$ million.

This page presents market research on Singapore's factory and business park sectors, featuring Exhibit 6-1 (a table of Net New and Potential Supply from 2014 to 2028F in '000 sq ft) and Exhibit 6-2 (a table of Notable Upcoming Completions from 2025 to 2027 in sq ft). The content details supply growth trends, occupancy data for private business parks, and upcoming project specifics without including audited portfolio statements, financial performance tables, or tenant mix data.

This page presents Exhibit 6-3, a dual-axis chart and table detailing the net demand and occupancy rates of business park space in Singapore from 2014 to 1Q 2025, reporting figures in '000 sq ft and %. The data indicates that while annual net new demand averaged 0.7 million sq ft through 2023, quarterly occupancy declined from a peak of ~84% in 2017 to 75.9% in 1Q 2025 due to increased supply, with rental indices shown in Exhibit 6-4 rising to 121.7 in 1Q 2025.

This page presents market research on Singapore's private warehouse segment, featuring Exhibit 7-1 which details the net new and potential supply of warehouse space in '000 sq ft from 2014 to 2028F. The content also includes Exhibit 7-2 listing notable upcoming completions such as DSV Pearl and World Gate 2 with their respective GFA and expected completion years.

This page features Exhibit 7-3, a table and chart detailing net demand and occupancy rates for warehouse space from 2014 to 1Q 2025 in '000 sq ft and %, alongside Exhibit 7-4 showing the JTC rental index trend. The reporting unit is explicitly stated as '000 sq ft for area metrics and % for occupancy/rental indices.

This page presents Exhibit 6, a table and chart detailing the timeline of major Sydney infrastructure projects from 2018 to 2032 by total project cost in AUD$b. The data lists ten projects including the Sydney airport gateway link (2018–2020) at $85b and Harbourside redevelopment (2021–2027) at $85b, with costs ranging down to $10b for Sydney Metro West.

This page presents Exhibit 10, a table detailing past year lease transactions in the Australia property market research section, listing tenants such as MultiLit and Toshiba alongside their leased area, rent rates, and incentive percentages. It also includes textual analysis of vacancy trends in Macquarie Park from January 2024 to January 2025 and Exhibit 11, a chart displaying historical net absorption and vacancy data over that period.

This page details the future supply pipeline and rental performance of Macquarie Park, featuring Exhibit 12 (Development Pipeline) which lists five projects with their status, completion years, and approximate square footage ranging from 10,000 to 16,800 sqm. Additionally, Exhibit 13 presents a table comparing average prime net face rents across NSW markets as of April 2025, reporting Macquarie Park at A$470/sqm alongside competitors such as North Sydney at A$928/sqm.

This page presents market research on the Australia property market, specifically focusing on Macquarie Park, with **Exhibit 14** detailing current rental discounts for Macquarie Park compared to suburban markets like Parramatta and Chatswood. It further includes data tables and charts from **Exhibits 15 through 17** covering average net face rents by grade (Prime and Secondary) from 2014 to 2025, historical supply additions as a percentage of total stock from 2006 to 2026, and a prime office market outlook projecting net face rent, growth rates, incentives, and net effective rent from 2022 to 2029.

This page presents market research on the Bella Vista office sector, detailing a vacancy rate of 3.7% and average prime net face rents of A$424/sqm as of April 2025. The content includes comparative tables (Exhibit 20, Exhibit 21) showing Bella Vista's position relative to other NSW markets regarding vacancy percentages and rental averages, along with data on rental discounts against suburban competitors.

This page details investment activity and market yields for the SGX REIT's North shore portfolio, led by Exhibit 23: Average rents (A$/sqm) across Bella Vista, Macquarie Park, Chatswood, and Parramatta from April 2015 to April 2025. It further presents data on average prime yields by market as of April 2025 in Exhibit 24 and historical office transaction values (A$10m+) by precinct from 2014 to 2024 in Exhibit 25.

This page presents Exhibit 26, a table detailing Australia Property Market Research investment sales transactions from 2023-2024, listing properties such as those in Sydney and North Sydney with their sale prices in Australian dollars (A$), yields, net lettable area, price per square meter, weighted average lease expiry, purchasers, vendors, and sale dates. The data source is Knight Frank Australia, with specific notes defining WALE as Weighted Average Lease Expiry and the asterisk indicating net sale price.

The page presents Exhibit 28, a table detailing industrial sale transactions in the Gold Coast region including property details, prices in Australian dollars (A$), yields, NLA square meters, and purchaser/vendor information. This is followed by Section 5.3 Outlook, which analyzes market growth drivers, rental demand trends for specific asset sizes, and constraints related to land availability and regional competition with Brisbane.

This page presents the AA REIT Sustainability Framework, detailing its FY2023–2025 roadmap aligned with the Paris Agreement and UN SDGs through a table mapping four ESG pillars (Build a Sustainable Business, Act Responsibly, Promote Well-being, Operate Ethically) to specific material topics and selected global goals. It also includes Vision, Mission, and Enabler tables outlining the organization's strategic focus on industrial real estate solutions, sustainable long-term returns, and foundational characteristics like internal collaboration and responsible investments.

This page presents the SGX REIT's sustainability report, featuring a table detailing FY2024 targets and FY2025 achievements under "Energy and emissions" alongside short-, medium-, and long-term targets for solar capacity and green leases. No financial statements, portfolio data, or distribution highlights are present on this page.

This page of the AA REIT Sustainability Report presents a table and chart detailing Energy Consumption (MWh) and Energy Intensity (kWh/m² of GFA) by property category for FY2023, FY2024, and FY2025. It further includes a second table and chart reporting Scope 2 Carbon Emissions (tCO₂e) and Intensity (kgCO₂e/m²), alongside narrative data on total consumption increases, emission reductions against a FY2020 baseline, and disclosures regarding head office measurements and scope definitions.

This page presents AA REIT's Scope 3 Emission Breakdown as at 31 March 2025, reporting total emissions of 28,551.96 tCO<sub>2</sub>e with a year-on-year increase of 6%. The main artifact is a table detailing five emission categories where Downstream Leased Assets (Category 13) account for 79.28% of the total, followed by Capital Expenditure, Purchased Goods and Services, Fuel and Energy Related Activities, and Business Travel.

This page presents the SGX REIT's FY2024 to FY2025 CSR targets and achievements alongside a Profile of Our Workforce table detailing 37 permanent employees across Executives, Middle Management, and Senior Management categories as of March 31, 2025. The employment data is reported in absolute counts and percentages without any specified currency or reporting unit schema (e.g., SGD'000).

This page contains the GRI Content Index for AIMS APAC REIT's ("AA REIT") Sustainability Report covering the period 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025, utilizing GRI Standards 1, 2, and 3 without any sector-specific standards. It details reporting practices including organizational details, entities included, external assurance (not sought), activities, workers, governance structure, and critical concerns, explicitly stating that no schema-relevant data such as audited portfolio statements, financial highlights, or tenant tables are present.

This page details the Corporate Governance role of the ARCC Chairperson and summarizes FY2025 reviews, including an independent assessment of AA REIT's audited financial statements. The main content is a table describing the Key Audit Matter regarding "Valuation of investment properties," which was addressed by reviewing external valuations conducted by independent professional valuers with appropriate qualifications as at 31 March 2025.

This page contains the Report of the Trustee for AIMS APAC REIT, confirming that HSBC Institutional Trust Services (Singapore) Limited has monitored the Manager's compliance with the Trust Deed during the year ended 31 March 2025. No schema-relevant data is present on this page.

This page contains the Independent Auditors' Report opinion confirming that AIMS APAC REIT's financial statements as at 31 March 2025 are fairly presented in accordance with RAP 7, specifically referencing the Statement of Portfolio (property valuations) and Statement of Total Return. The report highlights key audit matters regarding the fair value valuation of the Group's twenty-four Singapore properties, two Australian properties, and a 49% joint venture interest in Australia, without presenting any audited tables or specific financial data.

This page presents the Statements of Financial Position for SGX REIT as at 31 March 2025, reporting Group and Trust balances in SGD'000 with total assets of SGD 2,290,620'000 (Group) and SGD 2,040,330'000 (Trust). The table details non-current and current assets including investment properties and cash equivalents, alongside liabilities such as interest-bearing borrowings and lease obligations, concluding with unitholders' funds of SGD 1,005,891'000 and a net asset value per unit attributable to unitholders of SGD 1.23.

This page presents the **Statement of Total Return** for SGX REIT for the year ended 31 March 2025, reporting Group and Trust total returns in SGD'000. The table details revenue components including gross revenue ($186,626 SGD'000), property operating expenses, borrowing costs, manager fees, fair-value changes on investment properties and derivatives, and tax impacts, culminating in total return after income tax attributable to Unitholders and Perpetual Securities holders.

This page presents the Distribution Statements for SGX REIT (SGD'000) covering the year ended 31 March 2025, detailing total return before tax of SGD 49,067 and net distributions to Unitholders of SGD 97,393. The table explicitly lists distribution amounts available at the beginning and end of the year, along with specific per-Unit payout rates ranging from 0.510 cents to 2.400 cents across various periods in 2023 and 2024.

This page contains the "Net effect of tax adjustments" table (Note A) and "Other adjustments" text (Note B) for the SGX REIT Trust, reporting financial data in $'000. The table details specific line items including amortisation of borrowing costs, manager fees, fair-value changes on investment properties and derivatives, interest expense, and various tax adjustments for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024.

This page presents the Statements of Movements in Unitholders' Funds and Perpetual Securities holders' funds for the year ended 31 March 2025, reporting Group and Trust balances in SGD'000. The table details total returns after income tax attributable to unitholders ($53,456k), net increases from operations, foreign currency translation reserves, hedging reserve changes, unitholder contributions including management fees and private placements, distributions, and issuance costs.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) for SGX REIT as at 31 March 2025, detailing 18 investment properties in Singapore with their locations, land lease terms, remaining lease durations, and existing uses. The table explicitly lists Group and Trust holdings across logistics, warehouse, hi-tech, business park, and industrial sectors without including financial metrics such as revenue, expenses, or distribution data.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations) for SGX REIT, detailing occupancy rates and carrying values in SGD'000 alongside group and trust percentages of total Unitholders' funds for 2025 and 2024.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for SGX REIT as at 31 March 2025, detailing investment properties in Singapore (including 3 Toh Tuck Link reclassified to held for sale) and Australia via Woolworths HQ and Boardriders Asia Pacific HQ. The table lists property locations, land lease terms, remaining lease durations, existing uses, and valuation notes indicating fair value adjustments for the divested Singapore asset and AUD-to-SGD conversions for Australian holdings.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement of property valuations, detailing 2024 and 2025 data for occupancy rates, carrying values in SGD'000 (ranging from $13,500 to $1,874,519), and group/trust percentages of total Unitholders' funds. The table concludes with a note stating that accompanying notes form an integral part of these financial statements.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement as at 31 March 2025, detailing investment properties and a joint venture in Australia including the Optus Centre. The reporting unit uses SGD'000 for financial figures, with specific notes clarifying valuation methods and the proposed divestment of the 3 Toh Tuck Link property at S$24.388 million.

This page presents a table of audited Portfolio Statement property valuations for the SGX REIT, reporting carrying values and group percentages in SGD'000. The data includes occupancy rates of 100% for both 2024 and 2025, along with detailed breakdowns of gross revenue, expenses, finance costs, fair-value changes, and tax impacts across the specified periods.

This page presents the **audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations)** for SGX REIT as at 31 March 2025, detailing carrying values in SGD'000 and trust percentages of total Unitholders' funds across investment properties, right-of-use assets, and other net assets. The report confirms that property valuations are based on independent full valuations by firms such as Jones Lang LaSalle Property Consultants Pte Ltd for Singapore properties, with specific footnotes noting a reclassification of the 3 Toh Tuck Link asset to investment property held for sale at fair value based on an agreed third-party sale price.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows for the year ended 31 March 2025, reporting SG$'000 values for cash flows from operating activities (including total return after income tax and adjustments), investing activities, and financing activities. The table details net cash used in financing activities of (SG$'000)111,508 due to distributions and repayments, resulting in a net decrease in cash and cash equivalents of (SG$'000)3,132, with end-of-year balances at SG$'00014,456.

This page presents the Significant non-cash transactions section of the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows for SGX REIT (SGD'000) year ended 31 March 2025, detailing new Units issued as partial payments for management fees and performance fees. The reporting unit is SGD'000.
This page contains no schema-relevant data.

This page contains accounting policy notes regarding the consolidation of joint ventures, elimination of intra-group transactions, foreign currency translation rules for Group entities and foreign operations, and recognition of foreign currency differences within the Statement of Total Return. No schema-relevant data such as audited portfolio statements, financial highlights, or tenant tables are present on this page.

This page of the SGX REIT annual report for the year ended 31 March 2025 details the accounting policies for foreign operations and investment properties, specifying that fair value changes are recognised directly in the statement of total return. The reporting unit is stated as SGD'000, with no audited Portfolio Statement, revenue/expense tables, tenant mix, or financial highlights present on this page.

This page details the accounting policies for plant and equipment, including recognition, measurement, subsequent costs, and depreciation methods applied to systems with useful lives over 18 to 20 years. No schema-relevant data such as audited Portfolio Statements, Total Return statements, or financial highlights are present.

This page details the Group's accounting policies for financial instruments, specifically covering derecognition criteria, offsetting rules, and hedge accounting mechanics for derivatives related to interest rate and foreign currency risks. The text explicitly states that changes in fair value for derivatives are generally recognised in the statement of total return unless designated within a qualifying hedge relationship.

This page of the SGX REIT annual report for the year ended 31 March 2025 contains no schema-relevant data, as it exclusively details accounting policies regarding derivative financial instruments and impairment provisions without presenting any audited Portfolio Statement, Statement of Total Return, revenue/expenses/fees tables, tenant information, or financial highlights.
This page of the SGX REIT annual report for the year ended 31 March 2025 contains accounting policy notes regarding impairment and leases without any schema-relevant data.

This page details the accounting policies for income tax expense under the Notes to the Financial Statements, specifying that current and deferred taxes are recognized in the Statement of Total Return except where items relate directly to Unitholders' funds. It outlines the Group's treatment of interest and penalties as provisions under FRS 37, describes criteria for recognizing deferred tax assets and liabilities, and explains the "tax transparency" ruling with IRAS regarding distributions without deducting income tax.

This page details the Group's and Trust's investment property balances as of 31 March 2025 (reported in $'000), including movements such as capital expenditure, fair value changes recognized in the statement of total return, and foreign currency translation. It also discloses the divestment of a leasehold property at 541 Yishun Industrial Park A in Singapore, completed on 12 September 2023 for $12.88 million.

This page details the fair value hierarchy and security status of investment properties for the SGX REIT group as at 31 March 2025, reporting values in SGD'000. This page contains the Level 3 fair value measurement disclosures and significant unobservable inputs for investment properties as at 31 March 2025, detailing valuation techniques such as discounted cash flow analysis and capitalisation methods along with their respective key assumptions. The reporting unit is expressed in SGD'000, though no specific table artifacts like audited Portfolio Statements, Top-N tenants, or financial highlights are present on this page.

This page presents Notes 5 and 6 detailing the Group's Plant and Equipment (specifically rooftop solar installations at 6 properties) and Subsidiaries, reporting all financial figures in SGD'000. The main artifact is the Plant and Equipment table showing a net book value of $13,381,000 as at 31 March 2025, while Note 6 discloses an impairment loss of $39,900 recognised in the statements of total return with no impact on distributable income.

This page presents the Subsidiaries table listing 10 entities with their incorporation countries, principal activities, and effective equity interests held by the Group for years 2025 and 2024, alongside a Joint Venture table detailing investment amounts and loan balances reported in SGD'000.

The accompanying financial information table for MPT reports revenue of \$36.3 million and a total loss of \$42.0 million for the year ended 31 March 2025, with property valuations confirmed by CBRE Valuations Pty Limited.

This page of the SGX REIT annual report for the year ended 31 March 2025 contains no schema-relevant data, as it details financial notes on joint ventures and trade receivables without including any audited portfolio statements, profit or loss tables, revenue/expenses/fees breakdowns, tenant mix information, distribution highlights, or manager/trustee/sponsor details.

This page presents a table of Derivative Financial Instruments (interest rate swaps and currency forward contracts) for the Group and Trust, reporting values in SGD'000 for years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024. The accompanying notes detail the Group's and Trust's use of these instruments to hedge floating rate loans by swapping interest expenses to fixed rates, specifying notional amounts, tenors, and specific fixed interest rates applied.

The primary table, titled "Hedging reserve" under Section 9 Derivative Financial Instruments (Cont'd), reports fair value gains/losses and reclassifications in USD'000 for both entities as of March 2024 and 2025, while a subsequent table under Section 10 Cash and Cash Equivalents lists bank balances also in USD'000.

This page presents the audited financial notes for Trade and Other Payables (Note 11) totaling $72,864,000 for the Group and $71,585,000 for the Trust as of 31 March 2025, alongside a detailed breakdown of Interest-Bearing Borrowings (Note 12) with a total Group balance of $578,743,000. The data explicitly details specific liability components including trade payables, deferred consideration related to electricity systems, and secured/unsecured bank borrowings presented in SGD'000.

This page presents detailed notes on interest-bearing borrowings for the year ended 31 March 2025, specifically outlining credit facilities, sustainability-linked loans, subsidiary term loans, and medium-term notes with amounts reported in SGD'000 and AUD. No audited Portfolio Statement, Statement of Total Return, DPU highlights, or tenant/customer tables are present on this page.

This page presents a detailed table of interest-bearing borrowings for the SGX REIT Group and Trust as of 31 March 2025, listing nominal values, carrying amounts, interest rates (BBSY or SORA based), maturity dates, and repayment schedules in SGD'000.
